## 2026-08-14 Control Instance Cycle and Service Attestation Runtime 0.1.122

- Synchronized the GovernanceObject bootstrap baseline from `GovernanceObject_2026-08-14-02.yml`, including ControlObjective `ZRM-ControlCycle` and `ZRM-Service`.
- Added an authoritative ConfigItem `Control` seed derived from `ConfigItem_2026-08-14-01.yml`. Bootstrap imports missing structure and merges only missing class/role definition structure; existing customer values and layout win.
- Added the exported Ticket Dynamic Fields `ZRM-Query`, `ZRM-Response`, and multi-row Set `Attestation` non-destructively.
- ControlObjective holds reusable frequency/service/program truth. ConfigItem `Control` holds runtime `ZRM-LastRun`, `ZRM-Result`, its ControlObjective reference, and its CI/GO/Ticket/MELT target reference.
- Added `NEW @TICKET`, ticket assignments, Attestation list/index assignments, `SUBMIT`, and deferred `EXPECT ... THEN PASS|FAIL|N/A ELSE ...` parsing.
- `NEW @TICKET` injects ServiceID exclusively from ControlObjective `ZRM-Service`; policy assignments populate the initial request and `SUBMIT` hands it to the existing Service Request workflow. No service is hardcoded in policy or runtime.
- Added `ZRMControlEvaluate` TransitionAction. The service workflow passes its current Ticket and exact ConfigItem Control ID; the action evaluates `EXPECT` and writes Pass/Fail/N/A directly to that Control instance.
- `ZRM-TKInstance` remains a control target reference and is not repurposed as an attestation-ticket link.
- Pass/Fail/N/A is result recording, not implicit remediation. Fail creates no additional work unless the policy explicitly defines a separate conditional failure action; automatic fail-ticket routing was rejected.
- Added cycle parsing for `N day/week/month/year N time(s)` and daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/annual names. Missing or unsupported cycles remain UNKNOWN/fail-closed.
- Added parser/evaluation, cycle, and non-destructive merge regression tests.

## 2026-08-14 OSCAL Control Version Inheritance 0.1.118

- Retained idempotent matching by GovernanceObject class plus Annex plus Version: an identical identity updates the existing record, while a different Version creates a distinct GovernanceObject with its own GovernanceID.

## 2026-08-13 OSCAL Policy Fan-Out Import Interface

- Added an agent-facing `OSCAL Policy Import` interface under GovernanceDB with JSON file upload/paste, preview, warnings, per-class counts, and explicit confirmed import.
- Added `Kernel::System::GovernanceObject::OSCALImport` as the mapping/orchestration service. The OSCAL catalog becomes the parent `Policy`; each OSCAL group/domain becomes a child `Policy`; each supplied control risk becomes a `RiskStatement`; and each control becomes a `ControlObjective`.
- Mapping follows the 2026-08-13 authoritative Governance Object export: catalog title becomes the parent Policy name; group title becomes child Policy name; group ID becomes child Policy annex; group overview becomes child Policy description; and `ZRM-Parent` links the domain through portable `Policy: Name` identity. Control title becomes ControlObjective and RiskStatement name; control ID becomes `ZRM-Annex`; risk prose becomes RiskStatement description; statement and guidance become labeled ControlObjective description sections and retain their corresponding policy filter/evaluation fields.
- Generated relationships use portable `Class: Name` values (`Policy: ...`, `RiskStatement: ...`) and resolve through the Governance Object document importer on the target instance.
- OSCAL group title is preserved in `ZRM-ControlClass`. It is deliberately not written to `ZRM-ControlCategory`, whose TESSERA vocabulary is People/Process/Technology/Data and has no authoritative OSCAL mapping.
- TESSERA likelihood/impact factors and control type are not invented when OSCAL omits them; model defaults remain authoritative.
- Import is idempotent by Governance Object class plus name: repeat imports update existing objects and create only new controls. Preview state is cached per user for one hour and import remains challenge-token protected.
- The included GovTech IM8 catalog validates at one parent Policy, 15 child domain Policies, 137 controls, and 137 risk statements. Controls and risks reference their domain Policy. The focused test verifies parent-child Policy mapping, AS-1 mapping, descriptions, portable references, and non-invention of TESSERA-only classifications.

## 2026-08-11 GovernanceDB 0.1.101 Package Recovery

### Runtime evidence and root causes

- The first 0.1.100 OPM omitted `Encode="Base64"` from every embedded payload. OTOBO consequently installed Base64 text as source files, producing the widespread `Identifier too long ... line 1` and dependent module-load failures.
- The missing SysConfig `Init` diagnostic was a consequence of the incorrectly extracted Base64 XML payload; all GovernanceDB source XML files have a valid `Framework`, `Application`, `Config`, or `Changes` init value.
- `governance_object_activity_article` exceeded OTOBO's 30-character table-name limit.
- The failed upgrade had already created `ztsm_configitem_activity`, so a blind retry of the same upgrade table operation was unsafe.

### Completed recovery

- Corrected OPM generation so all 242 payloads declare `Encode="Base64"` and decode byte-for-byte to their package sources.
- Shortened the separate GovernanceObject table to `governance_object_activity` without changing its object ownership or semantics.
- Kept activity tables in the fresh-install schema, removed their non-idempotent upgrade declarations, and added bootstrap table discovery that creates only a missing activity table. This supports retry after the observed partial 0.1.100 failure.

### Validation

- Released the recovery as `0.1.101` so Package Manager can upgrade whether the failed attempt retained registry version 0.1.99 or 0.1.100.
- GovernanceDB `0.1.101` contains 242 byte-verified payloads, zero mismatches, and zero missing Base64 encoding declarations.
- SHA256: `0F7AF76714D285633FC7D4335867122672C63BE5D5373CF312C0DF70B3B60F2E`.
- GovernanceDB source XML, SOPM, generated OPM, bootstrap Perl, activity Perl, and focused tests pass validation.

## 2026-08-11 Object-Owned Activity Articles

### Completed work

- Added rich Activity Articles independently to ConfigItem, GovernanceObject, and MELTObject. Each object family has its own table, system adapter, event recorder, frontend action, and article list.
- Preserved the existing short technical history recorders. Activity Articles are additive and use later `110-TESSERAActivityArticles` event modules; they do not replace the existing history modules.
- Structured ConfigItem imports create an additional readable activity snapshot identifying YAML/JSON or Excel as the source.
- Preserved strict ownership: GovernanceDB owns ConfigItem and GovernanceObject activity implementations; MELT owns only MELTObject activity implementation. No object is copied, migrated, renamed, or retyped.

### Architectural decisions

- An Activity Article is immutable execution/audit evidence owned by its subject object. Similar behavior is duplicated through object-specific adapters, not implemented by converting one object family into another.
- Technical history and readable Activity Articles serve different purposes and remain side by side.

### Validation

- Added `scripts/test/TESSERA/ObjectActivityArticles.t` to verify separate tables, separate event recorders, visible actions, and preservation of the original MELT history registration.

## 2026-08-11 CMDB Data Actions and Workbook 0.1.100

### Completed work

- Duplicated the established action-row capabilities onto the agent CMDB overview without changing the GovernanceObject actions: Bulk, ConfigItem YAML/JSON, General Catalog YAML/JSON, and Excel Import/Export.
- General Catalog YAML/JSON now accepts `AgentITSMConfigItem` as a safe return target, while retaining the existing GovernanceObject and admin return paths.
- Added a ConfigItem-owned YAML/JSON codec and frontend; it resolves runtime ConfigItem class definitions and does not reuse GovernanceObject persistence.
- Added genuine XLSX export/import using the packaged SheetJS runtime. Every active ConfigItem class receives its own worksheet and every asset occupies one row.
- Export headers are generated from current class definitions. Structured, Set, Group, and multi-value values remain one JSON cell rather than numbered columns.
- Added class-specific `Download empty template` and `Export class assets` actions. The selected class defaults from the CMDB class page when available.
- Template columns walk the effective `DefinitionRef` returned by `DefinitionGet()`, after referenced role definitions have been expanded, so the spreadsheet follows the actual class-page form instead of a static field list.
- Added preview-token-gated commit. Every row requires explicit Create, Update, or Skip; imports do not silently overwrite.
- When an update would clear previously populated values, preview identifies the fields and requires the separate `UPDATE_CLEAR` decision plus a browser confirmation.
- Missing ConfigItem Number plus a matching Name/Application/Environment/Location tuple produces `REVIEW_SAME_ASSET`. The tuple comparison is case-insensitive; CMDB Number remains exact.
- Added configurable `TESSERA::CMDB::VirtualAssetTag###Pattern`, defaulting to `<ZTSM-Code>-VT-<running id>`. The code is resolved from the referenced Application GovernanceObject and ConfigItemID supplies the monotonic running ID.

### Validation

- New and modified Perl modules pass syntax validation.
- GovernanceDB SysConfig XML parses successfully.
- Both new JavaScript modules pass Node syntax validation.
- Added `scripts/test/TESSERA/ConfigItemDataActions.t` for action, duplicate-rule, workbook, and virtual-tag invariants.

### Architectural decisions

- Human-readable names are workbook/document identity; numeric database identifiers are not exposed as authored reference identity.
- Duplicate reconciliation is advisory and case-insensitive across the four business identity fields. It never implies an automatic merge when CMDB Number is absent.
- Virtual-tag generation fails closed when the Application or its exact `ZTSM-Code` cannot be resolved.

## 2026-08-11 CMDB Action-Row Script Loader Restoration 0.1.99

### Runtime evidence

- Browser console confirmed both required configuration structures are present and populated:
  - `Core.Config.Get('ITSMConfigItemActionRow')`;
  - `Core.Config.Get('ITSMConfigItem').ConfigItemActionRow`.
- Therefore the repeated `reading 'ConfigItemActionRow'` exception is not missing row data. It is the dereference of the missing `ITSM.UI.ConfigItemActionRow` JavaScript namespace inside `ITSM.Agent.ConfigItem.Overview`.

### Completed work

- Bumped GovernanceDB to `0.1.99`.
- Corrected `_CustomerAssetFrontendEnsure()` so every install/upgrade explicitly injects `ITSM.UI.ConfigItemActionRow.js` into the effective `AgentITSMConfigItem` module loader immediately before the guard and overview script.
- The bootstrap removes stale/duplicate occurrences first, making the resulting order deterministic:
  1. `ITSM.UI.ConfigItemActionRow.js`;
  2. `ZTSM.Agent.ConfigItem.OverviewGuard.js`;
  3. `ITSM.Agent.ConfigItem.Overview.js`.
- This repairs deployed SysConfig state even when the source XML already contains the correct script but the live effective loader value lost it.

### Validation

- GovernanceDB bootstrap passes Perl syntax validation.
- Built `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.99.opm` with 227 verified payloads and zero payload mismatches.
- SHA256: `A3593F74F7F7C9BAE57205E0EE53FC81AEDD62F4BF24194ED7E89E0B29AD8556`.

## 2026-08-11 MELT Cross-Object Rewrite Removal 0.0.8

### Root cause

- Confirmed the early MELT compatibility bridge was still present in the current bootstrap and could mutate globally named Dynamic Fields owned by ConfigItem, GovernanceObject, Ticket, or CustomerUser.
- `_DynamicFieldsEnsure()` resolved fields by global name and force-updated collisions to `ObjectType => MELTObject`, including a direct SQL fallback. This directly explains the deployed `*Old` MELTObject fields followed by reimported GovernanceObject replacements.
- Additional inherited bridge methods could rewrite Ticket reference drivers and stored reference IDs, copy ConfigItems into MELT, and delete MELT runtime records during package upgrade.

### Completed work

- Bumped MELT to `0.0.8`.
- Removed the `Kernel::System::ITSMConfigItem` bootstrap dependency.
- Disabled all inherited ConfigItem/Ticket migration bridges:
  - `_TicketReferenceValuesRepair()`;
  - `_TicketReferenceDynamicFieldsRepair()`;
  - `_ConfigItemsCopyToMELTObjects()`.
- Converted `CopiedObjectDataClear()` into a compatibility no-op so MELT upgrades never delete runtime objects or evidence.
- Added strict Dynamic Field ownership boundaries:
  - MELT class-field maintenance skips any existing field whose `ObjectType` is not `MELTObject`.
  - MELT customer-user maintenance skips existing fields unless they are already `CustomerUser/MELTObject` fields.
  - MELT definition snapshots now accept only valid `MELTObject` fields and exclude included fields owned by other object types.
- Preserved all ConfigItem and GovernanceObject modules, templates, SysConfig, and package file ownership outside MELT.

### Architectural decisions

- MELT is a standalone evidence/object database. It must not migrate, copy, rename, retype, repair, or delete ConfigItem, GovernanceObject, Ticket, or CustomerUser data.
- A global Dynamic Field name collision is fail-closed: MELT logs and skips the field. It never takes ownership from another object type.
- MELT forms may use only fields genuinely owned by `MELTObject`; a cloned definition is not authority to capture another package's Dynamic Field.
- The old compatibility methods remain as inert entry points for upgrade compatibility, but their cross-object behavior is permanently disabled.

### Validation

- MELT bootstrap and MELTObject definition modules pass Perl syntax validation.
- MELT `0.0.8` has 96 verified payloads with zero payload mismatches.
- MELT file ownership overlap is zero against both GovernanceDB `0.1.98` and the authoritative ITSMConfigurationManagement package.
- No ConfigItem dependency, Ticket reference-ID update SQL, external reference-driver rewrite, or upgrade table-delete loop remains in the MELT bootstrap.
- Built `Kernel/Package/MELT-0.0.8.opm`.
- SHA256: `24B04B892D133A91B2A289ED2FFEADFBC62296CDA503946E250E4C987E011424`.

### Runtime recovery order

- Upgrade MELT to `0.0.8` first so it can no longer damage restored ownership.
- Upgrade/reinstall GovernanceDB `0.1.98` next so its authoritative bootstrap and CMDB overlay restore GovernanceObject and ConfigItem runtime registrations.
- Retain the `*Old` rows temporarily as recovery evidence; do not delete them until field ownership, values, and references have been reconciled from the latest exports.

## 2026-08-11 Initial ControlObjective Policy Engine 0.1.96

### Completed work

- Added the first fail-closed TESSERA policy interpreter in `Kernel::System::TESSERA::PolicyEngine`.
- Added `Kernel::System::GenericAgent::ZRMPolicyEvaluator`, which discovers `ControlObjective` GovernanceObjects by class name, evaluates `ZRM-PolicyFilter` for ticket applicability, and then evaluates `ZRM-PolicyEvaluation`.
- Policy outcomes are `SATISFIED`, `NOT_SATISFIED`, or `UNKNOWN`; missing fields, invalid conversions, ambiguous values, and unsupported grammar remain `UNKNOWN` and never establish control satisfaction.
- Added initial typed grammar for `@TICKET` and `@CONTROLOBJECTIVE` fields, explicit `NUMBER`, `STRING`, `DATE`, and `DATETIME` conversion, multiplication/division, `PRODUCT OF`, comparisons, Boolean line joins, `NOW`, and relative day/week/month/year expressions.
- Added an event-driven GenericAgent seed for ticket creation and Dynamic Field updates. Matching results are written as private ticket article evidence and deduplicated by evaluation digest.
- Added a fresh-install/upgrade-safe `ControlObjective` class definition using the exact exported `ZRM-PolicyFilter` and `ZRM-PolicyEvaluation` Dynamic Fields.
- Added `var/governancedb/policy/control_objective_examples.txt` containing separate applicability-filter and policy-evaluation samples.

### Architectural decisions

- Authored policy uses object, class, field, calendar, and catalog names; database IDs are not valid policy identity.
- `ZRM-PolicyFilter` controls applicability only. `ZRM-PolicyEvaluation` determines the Control Objective result only after applicability is satisfied.
- GenericAgent is the runtime trigger; ControlObjective remains governance truth and the ticket article remains execution evidence.
- The initial grammar is deliberately bounded. Reserved traversal, collection, scheduling, variable, business-calendar, ITSMConfigItem, and MELT syntax must return `UNKNOWN` until implemented.

### Validation

- Policy engine and GenericAgent modules pass Perl syntax checks.
- GenericAgent seed parses as YAML.
- Default class model parses as JSON and contains exactly one `ControlObjective` with both authoritative policy fields.
- Smoke evaluation passed for applicability, numeric `PRODUCT OF`, explicit conversion, and fail-closed missing-field behavior.
- Built `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.96.opm` with 225 payloads; every decoded payload matches its current package source.
- GovernanceDB `0.1.96` SHA256: `C85C6D665853D8F17FAB06B266A878D0665489F57F7345E167A51A10BBD48E53`.

### Architectural decisions

- OTOBO core is framework-owned and must remain upgradeable independently of GovernanceDB.
- GovernanceDB customizations of existing framework files belong under `$OTOBO_HOME/Custom`; direct core overwrites are prohibited for the 11.1 package line.
- New uniquely named GovernanceDB modules may remain normal package payload files because they do not replace framework files.
- PSGI or Apache must be restarted after installing/upgrading GovernanceDB so Perl modules under `Custom` are loaded.

### Known issues / runtime verification

- Install and upgrade must still be exercised in a running OTOBO 11.1 beta 2 environment with its database and companion packages.
- Retest customer ticket create/zoom, DynamicField Set administration/rendering, GenericAgent execution, process actions, and customer ConfigItem entitlement after restart.
- OTOBO 11.1 is still beta; a final 11.1 release compatibility audit remains required before production rollout.

## 2026-08-03 Customer Asset Access Enforcement Clarification

### Confirmed design

- Add a dedicated customer portal asset icon/navigation entry.
- The asset icon must be authorization-aware; it must not provide or imply asset access for every customer user merely because the customer ConfigItem frontend is enabled.
- Full asset list/detail access requires a matching `SupportAssignment` for the logged-in CustomerUser whose GovernanceRole is exactly `ASSET`.
- IPC membership, emergency IPC capabilities, customer company membership, ticket participation, and any other role or privilege must not bypass the `ASSET` requirement.
- Direct ConfigItem zoom URLs, version selection, and attachment/inline-content endpoints must enforce the same centralized backend authorization as the asset icon and asset list.
- Request-target discovery remains a separate entitlement boundary: where a workflow needs selectable assets, results are limited by ContractEntitlement and matching SupportProfile assignment, while full asset viewing still requires role `ASSET`.

### Initial read-only trace

- `CustomerITSMConfigItem` performs list and filter searches directly through `ConfigItemSearch` using the legacy `Customer::ConfigItem::PermissionConditions` model.
- `CustomerITSMConfigItemSearch` performs its own direct `ConfigItemSearch` calls.
- `CustomerITSMConfigItemZoom` and `CustomerITSMConfigItemAttachment` call the legacy `CustomerPermission` method, which can grant through generic group, class, Dynamic Field, CustomerUser, or customer-company conditions.
- The stock `CustomerFrontend::Navigation###CustomerITSMConfigItem###003-ITSMConfigItem` entry is static and cannot by itself enforce the new per-user SupportAssignment/`ASSET` authorization.
- No IPC or generic legacy customer permission path is acceptable as a fallback for the new asset-access surface.

### Current implementation direction

1. Add one centralized deny-by-default customer ConfigItem entitlement service.
2. Separate request-target discovery checks from `ASSET` list/detail checks.
3. Route customer list, search, zoom, version, attachment, and navigation visibility through that service.
4. Add bypass-focused automated tests before enabling portal UI.

## 2026-07-31 Confirmed Next Direction: Customer Portal Asset Entitlement

### Confirmed design

- Customer portal ConfigItem access will become a new first-class TESSERA feature; today customers do not have an accepted asset visibility model.
- The latest GovernanceObject, ConfigItem, and DynamicField exports are the design baseline for the next implementation session.
- The ConfigItem model introduces class `ContractEntitlement`.
- `ContractEntitlement` points to the applicable SupportProfile.
- Assets use the exported fields `ZTAM-ContractEntitlement` and `ZTAM-SupportProfile`.
- A CustomerUser may select, filter, search, or otherwise discover only assets whose SupportProfile is covered by ContractEntitlement and matches a SupportAssignment held by that CustomerUser.
- Assets outside that entitlement boundary must remain undiscoverable through every route, including direct IDs, crafted requests, alternative listings, autocomplete, search, and filter endpoints.
- Full ConfigItem detail visibility requires a matching SupportAssignment whose GovernanceRole is `ASSET`.
- `ASSET` is a new GovernanceRole value.
- Discovery/selection eligibility and full-detail visibility are deliberately separate permissions: entitlement makes an asset an eligible request target; the `ASSET` role grants access to all asset information.
- Customer company membership, ticket association, knowledge of an asset identifier, and frontend-only hiding do not independently grant ConfigItem access.
- Missing or ambiguous entitlement resolution must fail closed.

### Export-aligned field names

- `ZTAM-ContractEntitlement`
- `ZTAM-SupportProfile`
- `Contract-ServiceProfile`
- `Contract-Coverage`
- `Contract-SupportProfie`
- `ZTSMSupportAssignment-UserAccount`
- `ZTSMSupportAssignment-SupportProfile`
- `ZTSMSupportAssignment-Role`

`Contract-SupportProfie` is recorded with the exact spelling present in the latest ConfigItem export. Implementation must not silently invent a corrected field name.

### Next implementation sequence

1. Trace all customer-facing ConfigItem selection, autocomplete, filter, search, list, zoom, and direct object access paths.
2. Define one centralized backend entitlement and detail-permission service.
3. Resolve CustomerUser SupportAssignments and their SupportProfiles using the exported governance model.
4. Resolve asset ContractEntitlement and SupportProfile relationships using the exported ConfigItem model.
5. Apply entitlement filtering to every discovery path before results are returned.
6. Apply GovernanceRole `ASSET` authorization to ConfigItem detail access.
7. Add portal UI only after backend enforcement is consistent.
8. Add bypass-focused tests for direct URLs, crafted identifiers, alternate endpoints, stale references, missing assignments, inactive/ambiguous records, and users entitled without the `ASSET` role.
9. Package the feature with idempotent fresh-install, upgrade, and reinstall behavior.

### Explicitly deferred

- No customer ConfigItem runtime implementation was started on 2026-07-31.
- No portal screens, permission modules, routing, package bootstrap changes, or migrations for this feature have yet been designed or accepted.
- Implementation is intentionally deferred to the next work session so it begins from this recorded contract and the latest exports.

## 2026-07-27 Change Request Execution Plan Runtime 0.1.37

### Completed work

- Added `Kernel::System::GenericAgent::ZTSMChangeTaskReader` as a change-specific execution reader separate from StateBook and BlueBook readers.
- Added exact parsing for the exported multi-value change plan fields:
  - `ZCH-Precheck`
  - `ZCH-Implementation`
  - `ZCH-PostChange`
  - `ZCH-Rollback`
- Added idempotent child identity using existing execution evidence fields:
  - `ZTicket-Parent`
  - `ZTicket-Stage = change-<phase>`
  - `ZTicket-BlueLevel`
  - `ZTicket-Chapter = ZCH-Seq`
- Added field propagation:
  - `ZCH-ScheduleStart` to `ZTicket-ScheduleStart`
  - `ZCH-ScheduleFinish` to `ZTicket-ScheduleFinish`
  - `ZCH-Profile` to `ZTicket-Profile` and `ZTicket-OwnerGroup`
  - `ZCH-Owner` to `ZTicket-Owner`
  - `ZCH-Weightage` to `ZTicket-RequiredWeightage` and `ZTicket-OwnerWeightage`
  - mandatory, strict, level, and sequence execution controls
- Added execution semantics:
  - mandatory rows must close successfully before their level is complete;
  - non-mandatory rows do not block progression when open or unsuccessful;
  - strict rows are generated only after `ZCH-ScheduleStart`;
  - non-strict rows generate as soon as the preceding mandatory level is complete;
  - scheduled non-mandatory rows must still be generated before the complete change plan releases the parent.
- Added direct SupportProfile assignment behavior:
  - no profile derivation or substitution is performed;
  - an explicit `ZCH-Owner` must have a matching SupportAssignment membership for the exact `ZCH-Profile`;
  - invalid owner/profile combinations are rejected with parent-ticket evidence.
- Added shared rollback behavior:
  - any unsuccessful mandatory Pre-check, Implementation, or Post-change child activates the same `ZCH-Rollback` plan;
  - normal change lifecycle progression stops while rollback is active;
  - successful mandatory rollback execution closes the parent Change Request as `closed rollback`;
  - StateBook does not resume after rollback.
- Added child and parent orchestration articles following the existing BlueBook evidence style.
- Extended `ZTSMBlueBookComplete` so the final in-progress BlueBook level cannot release a Change Request until its change execution plan is also complete.
- Added event-driven and every-minute scheduled GenericAgent jobs so strict scheduled tasks are generated even when no ticket event occurs at the scheduled time.
- Added upgrade-safe bootstrap definitions for all exported `ZCH-*` component and Set Dynamic Fields, using class names rather than environment-specific GeneralCatalog IDs.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` from `0.1.36` to `0.1.37`.
- Generated `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.37.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.37.opm` SHA256: `5357F3CDE6EA5B3B66DF7082ABFD3EE19C13AA0A71314E32E120228F4AC23A83`.

### Architectural decisions

- Change Request task plans are execution choreography owned by the Change Request, not StateBook transitions and not BlueBook records.
- The normal in-progress BlueBook remains active. Final StateBook continuation requires both the normal BlueBook and the change-specific plan to complete.
- Change children use existing execution evidence fields for identity; no unconfirmed lifecycle or marker Dynamic Field was invented.
- Rollback follows the configured rollback levels and sequences rather than inferring a reverse implementation order.
- Schedule arrival is handled by a recurring reader scan because event-only execution cannot observe time passing.

### Rejected approaches

- Do not extend `ZTSMBlueBookReader` to parse `ZCH-*` rows.
- Do not copy environment-specific GovernanceObject class/status IDs from the Dynamic Field export into package bootstrap.
- Do not resolve a substitute SupportProfile when `ZCH-Profile` is configured.
- Do not allow a mandatory unsuccessful change child to advance normal execution.
- Do not resume StateBook after a completed rollback.

  - `ZTSMChangeTaskReader.pm`

  - `GovernanceDB::Bootstrap.pm`

### Architectural decisions

- Hostname policy is row-scoped for provisioning records, not ticket-scoped.
- `ZTicket-Custom` remains an input segment inside `ZCompute-VM`.
- `ZTicket-Hostname` is the generated output field inside `ZCompute-VM` and is the future CMDB automation binding key.
- When global hostname policy is disabled, row-local `ZTicket-Custom` becomes that row's complete hostname and is written into row-local `ZTicket-Hostname`.
- When global hostname policy is enabled, configured segments are resolved per row and written into row-local `ZTicket-Hostname`.

## 2026-07-21 Provisioning Hostname Policy 0.0.363

### Completed work

- Added SysConfig `ZTSM::Provisioning::HostnamePolicy`.
- Policy supports global enforcement on/off:
  - When enforcement is off, `ZTicket-Custom` is treated as the provided hostname.
  - When enforcement is on, fields with position greater than `0` are resolved and joined in position order.
- Added default configurable segment positions for:
  - `ZTicket-Location`
  - `ZTicket-Environment`
  - `ZTicket-Application`
  - `ZTicket-FunctionProfile`
  - `ZTicket-Custom`
  - `ZCompute-Image`
  - `ZCompute-CpuCore`
  - `ZCompute-GPU`
  - `ZCompute-RAM`
  - `ZStorage-FS`
  - `ZTicket-NetworkAdapter`
- Added code-field mapping defaults:
  - GovernanceObject references resolve `ZTSM-Code`.
  - ConfigItem references resolve `ZTAM-Code`.
  - `ZCompute-Image` explicitly resolves `ZTAM-Code`.
- Added bootstrap-created Ticket DynamicField `ZTicket-Custom` as a Text field.
- Added customer portal AJAX resolver `ZTSMHostnamePolicyResolve` in `CustomerTicketMessage`.
- Added service-form browser integration to send current provisioning field values, receive the resolved hostname, and store it in hidden submit field `ZTSMHostnamePolicyResolved` without overwriting `ZTicket-Custom`.
- Mirrored customer module/template changes across package source, runtime overlay, and `ZTSMOverlay`.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` package version to `0.0.363`.
- Generated `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.363.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.363.opm` SHA256: `801E6584FD6851E356837AC4BE787E3F3C4F5232FE69D95B26B765F15B67F6BF`.

### Architectural decisions

- Hostname policy is a provisioning/service-form concern, not a ticket-number identity concern.
- Segment position `0` disables that segment.
- `ZTicket-Custom` is deliberately not overwritten when global policy is enforced, because it remains the requester/operator custom segment.
- The generated hostname is exposed as `ZTSMHostnamePolicyResolved` for runtime/provisioning consumption.

## 2026-07-20 GovernanceDB Version Rollover Rule

### Completed work

- Recorded the package versioning decision in `AGENTS.md`.
- GovernanceDB `0.0.x` patch builds must stop at `0.0.365`.

## 2026-07-20 Reference Picker Container Anchor 0.0.345

### Completed work

- Corrected the `0.0.344` anchor attempt after runtime DOM showed why `+/-` still visually covered the picker:
  - The search picker was appended inside `.Field` before `.AddRemoveValueRow`.
  - OTOBO renders/updates `.AddRemoveValueRow` after the picker, so the later add/remove row can sit on top of the search trigger.

## 2026-07-15 Dynamic Field Group Source Implementation for Two-Depth Rows

### Completed work

- Added a new `DynamicFieldGroup` DynamicField driver as a Set-derived container that can be included inside an outer Dynamic Field Set.
- Kept existing Dynamic Field Set behavior stable by adding small extension hooks for field CSS/template class selection instead of changing Set storage semantics.
- Added nested parameter naming for Group render/value/validation state so inner controls are scoped by the group instance and outer row, avoiding collisions across repeated server rows.
- Added nested storage handling for Group inside Set:
  - outer Set index maps to `IndexSet`;
  - inner Group row index maps to `IndexValue`;
  - Group children are treated as storage multi-values only while nested inside a Set.
- Added `AdminDynamicFieldGroup` as a Set-admin derivative that rejects Set/Group children and rejects multi-value child fields, keeping this first implementation to a maximum of two row depths.
- Updated DynamicField included-field tracking so `UpdateSetFieldIncludedFields` applies to both `Set` and `DynamicFieldGroup`.
- Registered `DynamicFieldGroup` for Ticket and ITSMConfigItem in core DynamicFields config, and for Ticket, ITSMConfigItem, Article, and GovernanceObject through GovernanceDB config.
- Synced the new/changed runtime files into the GovernanceDB runtime overlay and added them to `GovernanceDB.sopm`.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` package version to `0.0.317`.
- Built `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.317.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.317.opm` SHA256: `13D95D7584BA13762CEE54AAD0C9DA0DE4AD2ADE85E8B30C8EE373FF751A83C8`.
- Supersedes `0.0.316`; use `0.0.317` for Dynamic Field Group install/upgrade testing.

### Architectural decisions

- Chose `DynamicFieldGroup` over a `DynamicFieldSchema` wrapper because the current Set driver already owns row storage, rendering, Include YAML validation, and DynamicField backend delegation.
- Group is allowed inside Set, but Group cannot contain Set or another Group. This gives the required two-depth shape without introducing unbounded recursive field containers.
- Multi-value child fields inside Group are rejected for now because Group-inside-Set uses the existing two-dimensional DynamicField storage axes. Supporting multi-value children would require a new three-dimensional storage contract.

### Validation

- Perl syntax checks passed for:
  - `Kernel/System/DynamicField/Driver/DynamicFieldGroup.pm`
  - `Kernel/Modules/AdminDynamicFieldGroup.pm`
  - `Kernel/System/DynamicField/Driver/Set.pm`
  - `Kernel/System/DynamicField/Event/UpdateSetFieldIncludedFields.pm`
  - matching GovernanceDB runtime-overlay copies.
- XML parse checks passed for:
  - `Kernel/Config/Files/XML/DynamicFields.xml`
  - `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB/Kernel/Config/Files/XML/GovernanceDB.xml`
  - `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB/GovernanceDB.sopm`
- Mirror hashes match for the touched source/runtime-overlay file pairs.
- Generated OPM parsed successfully as XML with package version `0.0.317`, file count `207`, and `missing_or_bad_base64=0`.
- Focused `git diff --check` passed for the touched Dynamic Field Group files and package metadata.

  - create an outer `DynamicFieldSet` that includes the group;
  - verify add/remove row behavior and submitted values on Ticket, ITSMConfigItem, and GovernanceObject surfaces.

## 2026-07-14 GovernanceDB 0.0.304 Incident Iteration Initialization and Confirmation Advancement

### Completed work

- Added an idempotent first-submission initializer in `CustomerTicketMessage`:
  - applies only when the submitted ticket type is `Incident`;
  - reads the existing `ZIN-Iteration` value directly from the Ticket DynamicField backend;
  - writes `ZIN-Iteration = 1` only when no value exists;
  - does not depend on `ZIN-Iteration` being visible or editable on the customer ticket form.
- Added an idempotent StateBook runtime repair for existing Incidents created before this fix:
  - initializes missing `ZIN-Iteration` to `1` before lifecycle orchestration continues;
  - updates the in-memory parent ticket so the same StateBook-to-BlueBook handoff immediately inherits iteration `1`;
  - leaves existing non-empty iteration values unchanged.
- Corrected unresolved Confirmation iteration advancement:
  - every Confirmation status other than a successful status advances the parent to the next iteration;
  - uses the Confirmation child ticket's `ZIN-Iteration` as the authoritative source when available;
  - uses iteration `1` as the legacy baseline when both child and parent values are missing, so the first failure writes `2`;
  - preserves a higher existing parent iteration and remains stable when the same Confirmation operation is retried.
- Treated both `Resolved` and `Auto-Confirmed` as successful Confirmation statuses:
  - closes the Confirmation ticket as `closed resolved`;
  - closes the parent Incident as `closed resolved`;
  - does not increment `ZIN-Iteration`.
- Synchronized `CustomerTicketMessage`, `CustomerTicketZTSMAction`, and `ZTSMStateBookReader` across canonical, package-source, GovernanceDB runtime-overlay, and ZTSMOverlay copies.
- Removed the completed parent-iteration initialization item from `PROJECT_NEXT.md`; child iteration propagation remains an active contract.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` to `0.0.304`.
- Rebuilt `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.304.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.304.opm` SHA256: `D240B527924E047413D3D61F46068D4E5B7C6C54BF3992DF2BBD37DF18102D95`.
- Supersedes `0.0.303`; use `0.0.304` for new Incident initialization, Confirmation failure loopback, `Auto-Confirmed`, and DIAGNOSE fan-out retesting.

### Architectural decisions

- Parent Incident iteration is system-owned execution context and is initialized after ticket creation, independently of customer-field visibility.
- StateBookReader provides the upgrade-safe runtime repair because existing Incident governance ledgers may predate the customer-submit initializer.
- A failed Confirmation advances from the Confirmation execution ledger's own iteration, preventing stale parent state from choosing the wrong next cycle.
- `Auto-Confirmed` is a successful terminal confirmation, equivalent to `Resolved` for closure and iteration behavior.

### Rejected approaches

- Do not rely on the customer form to submit `ZIN-Iteration`.
- Do not initialize every ticket type to iteration `1`; the first-submit initializer is Incident-specific.
- Do not use missing iteration plus one as `1` after a failed Confirmation; missing means the failed cycle was iteration `1`, so the next cycle is `2`.
- Do not increment again when retrying the same failed Confirmation after the parent already reached the calculated next iteration.

### Validation

- All eight active `CustomerTicketMessage.pm` and `CustomerTicketZTSMAction.pm` mirrors pass `perl -I. -IKernel/cpan-lib -c`.
- `CustomerTicketMessage.pm` mirrors share SHA256 `DC45F7D51926187C31CFED00F288C1E3A739F8346AC7741BC14EF346C010A19B`.
- `CustomerTicketZTSMAction.pm` mirrors share SHA256 `DBFEF0A8C58CCD4558BD1DB41B7FFFFFC1A847004D8B93EEF3FF1AC8A063615F`.
- `ZTSMStateBookReader.pm` mirrors share SHA256 `AF49412B4629B30523FAD35C516B5819088B4439D2A3569CC55D2482F519EC0E`.
- Generated OPM parses successfully as XML with package version `0.0.304`, file count `204`, and `MissingOrNonBase64=0`.
- Decoded OPM payload checks confirm Incident-only submission initialization, existing-Incident StateBook repair, in-memory handoff value `1`, Confirmation-child iteration sourcing, legacy failure advancement to `2`, retry stability, and `Auto-Confirmed` success handling.

## 2026-07-14 GovernanceDB 0.0.303 DIAGNOSE Evidence Routing and Assessment Fan-Out

### Completed work

- Corrected the `DIAGNOSE` GovernanceRole path in Generic Agent `ZTSMRoleDirector` so it no longer resolves through Support Assignment plus Application.
- Added closed Diagnosis evidence lookup using the same `ZTicket-Parent`, `TicketType = Diagnosis`, `StateType = closed`, and the same `ZIN-Iteration` first.
- Added `ZIN-Iteration - 1` fallback only when no closed Diagnosis tickets exist at the current iteration.
- Resolved `ZIN-Outcome` through the DynamicField backend before filtering, so stored catalog IDs and display values behave consistently.
- Excluded `Not Applicable` and `Recovered` outcomes from downstream ownership.
- Preserved distinct actionable Diagnosis `ZTicket-OwnerGroup` values in deterministic source-ticket order.
- Updated the original downstream ticket with the first diagnosis-derived SupportProfile.
- Added downstream ticket fan-out from index 1 onward:
  - creates one sibling for each additional distinct diagnosis-derived OwnerGroup;
  - copies the source ticket's core ticket data;
  - copies every valid Ticket DynamicField except `ZTicket-OwnerGroup`;
  - writes the target diagnosis-derived OwnerGroup after the copy.
- Added retry-safe duplicate prevention using ticket type, parent, iteration, BlueBook, chapter, and target OwnerGroup.
- Made retries preserve an already-valid diagnosis-derived SupportProfile while creating only missing sibling tickets.
- Synchronized Generic Agent `ZTSMRoleDirector` across canonical, package-source, GovernanceDB runtime-overlay, and ZTSMOverlay copies.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` to `0.0.303` and rebuilt `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.303.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.303.opm` SHA256: `8F673C6DB16DC7FDF509E8886BCB6DD0BD41966347F488D44A4E5F5293253B08`.
- Supersedes the `0.0.302` DIAGNOSE Support Assignment behavior; use `0.0.303` for the next DIAGNOSE routing and fan-out retest.

### Architectural decisions

- `DIAGNOSE` is an evidence-driven GovernanceRole directive, not a Support Assignment role lookup.
- Diagnosis ownership comes from closed Diagnosis execution ledgers sharing the downstream ticket's parent and iteration.
- The first owner group normalizes the existing downstream ticket; additional owner groups expand it into sibling execution tickets.
- Current-iteration closed Diagnosis evidence is authoritative. Previous-iteration fallback is allowed only when current-iteration closed Diagnosis tickets do not exist.
- Multiple actionable Diagnosis tickets with the same OwnerGroup produce one downstream ticket for that distinct operational scope.
- ChapterDirector remains outside owner-group resolution and downstream fan-out.

### Rejected approaches

- Do not resolve `DIAGNOSE` through `SupportAssignment` using GovernanceRole and Application.
- Do not select a single diagnosis winner and discard other actionable OwnerGroups.
- Do not fall back to the previous iteration merely because current outcomes are all non-actionable.
- Do not clone `ZTicket-OwnerGroup` from the source downstream ticket before assigning the diagnosis-derived value.

- Generated OPM parses successfully as XML with package version `0.0.303`, file count `204`, and `MissingOrNonBase64=0`.

- `ZTicket-OwnerGroup` is the operational assignment selector and is intentionally polymorphic.
- GovernanceRole-based assignment remains dynamic; it is not converted into a SupportProfile during child creation.
- `ZTicket-Profile` remains an execution snapshot for compatibility and is not used as the customer-permission ownership source.
- The BlueBook `ZBlue-Role` / child `ZTicket-Role` remains escalation and notification metadata and does not replace the OwnerGroup selector.

### Rejected approaches

- Do not leave `ZTicket-OwnerGroup` empty when GovernanceRole resolution has no immediate SupportProfile result.
- Do not force `ZTicket-OwnerGroup` to SupportProfile-only.
- Do not resolve a GovernanceRole without the ticket Application when Application context is present.
- Do not rely on the legacy RoleDirector to rewrite the OwnerGroup after child creation.

  - customer permission contains class-aware OwnerGroup assignment resolution with GovernanceRole and Application filters.

## 2026-07-14 GovernanceDB 0.0.300 Profile-Aware Dynamic Assignment

### Completed work

- Corrected BlueBook child assignment when `ZBlue-Profile` contains a `GovernanceRole` instead of a direct `SupportProfile`.
- Assignment now treats the polymorphic Profile field as the assignment source:
  - `SupportProfile` values resolve directly.
  - `GovernanceRole` values resolve through `SupportAssignment` using the parent `ZTicket-Application`.
- The separate `ZBlue-Role` field remains execution metadata and is no longer used as the fallback assignment role.
- GovernanceRole and Application text values are resolved by class and name before filtering; only numeric governance references are passed to GovernanceObject DynamicField searches.
- Synchronized the TransitionAction reader and reusable BlueBook runtime across canonical, package-source, GovernanceDB runtime-overlay, and ZTSMOverlay copies.

- Supersedes `0.0.299`; use `0.0.300` for the next Incident Assessment assignment retest.

### Architectural decisions

- `ZBlue-Profile` is intentionally polymorphic and remains the sole BlueBook assignment selector.
- Support Assignment determines operational scope only when the Profile value is a `GovernanceRole`.
- Human-readable governance names are accepted at the boundary, but GovernanceObject reference fields are always queried with numeric references.

### Rejected approaches

- Do not use `ZBlue-Role` such as `Primary` to replace a Profile value such as `DIAGNOSE`; these fields have different responsibilities.
- Do not send raw text such as `Primary` or `IaaS Ext` into GovernanceObject reference-field filters.

## 2026-07-14 GovernanceDB 0.0.295 Diagnosis Parent Severity Roll-Up

### Completed work

- Added Diagnosis-to-parent Incident severity roll-up in `CustomerTicketZTSMAction.pm`.
- On every Diagnosis submit, the runtime now:
  - reads the Diagnosis child ticket `ZTicket-Parent`;
  - loads the parent ticket with dynamic fields;
  - compares submitted child `ZIN-Severity` against parent `ZIN-Severity`;
  - treats smaller severity numbers as higher severity, for example `S1` higher than `S2`, `S2` higher than `S3`;
  - writes parent `ZIN-Severity` only when the child severity is higher than the current parent severity;
  - preserves the parent severity when the child severity is equal, lower, blank, or cannot be ranked.
- Blank parent severity is treated as updatable when the child submits a rankable severity.
- Added notice logging when Diagnosis severity roll-up updates the parent ticket.
- Synced `CustomerTicketZTSMAction.pm` across canonical runtime source, GovernanceDB package source, GovernanceDB runtime overlay, and `ZTSMOverlay`.

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.282 Follow-up Parent Handoff Fix

### Completed work

- Fixed follow-up child completion not returning the original DG/Diagnosis ticket from `follow-up` to `in-progress`.
- Root cause:
  - `_FollowUpApply` changed the original DG ticket to `follow-up`;
  - then it spawned the PurpleBook follow-up task under the root incident parent instead of under the DG ticket;
  - `CompleteTask` therefore evaluated the root incident as the handoff parent and never moved the DG ticket back to `in-progress`.

  - if the completed task's direct parent is not in `follow-up`, the submit path searches that parent's children for exactly one `follow-up` ticket whose resolved PurpleBook matches the completed task's BlueBook;

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.278 Follow-up Complete Button Gate Fix

- Fixed `Complete` disappearing from requester follow-up child tasks after the IPC `Patch` follow-up guard changes.

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.274 IPC Patch Permission Gate Fix

### Completed work

- Fixed the `Insufficient Rights / No Permission!` error when an IPC user submits the customer `Patch` recovery action.
- Root cause: `CustomerTicketZTSMAction` performed the normal customer `ro` permission check before the `Patch` branch could enforce IPC permission, so an IPC recovery user could see the menu action but be rejected on submit for tickets outside normal customer access.
- `CustomerTicketZTSMAction` now resolves IPC identity before the first ticket read gate.
- Emergency IPC actions `Patch`, `Delegate`, and `Override` can pass the first `ro` gate only when the user is IPC.
- The later action-specific checks remain in place:
  - `Patch` still requires IPC access;
  - acknowledgement, target state, remarks, state-type allowlist, and audit article remain mandatory;
  - the action still changes only ticket state and does not run StateBook, BlueBook, TransitionAction modules, chapter evaluation, orchestration, or governance recalculation.
- Synced `CustomerTicketZTSMAction.pm` across canonical runtime source, GovernanceDB package source, GovernanceDB runtime overlay, and `ZTSMOverlay`.

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.273 IPC Patch Ticket State Recovery

### Completed work

- Added an IPC-only `Patch` recovery action on `CustomerTicketZoom`.
- Purpose: allow IPC to manually correct a ticket state when a process/workflow bug leaves a ticket stranded outside the intended condition, for example an execution ticket stuck in `follow-up`.
- `Patch` is shown in the action menu for IPC users, including tickets currently in `follow-up`.
- The `Patch` dialog includes an explicit warning:
  - the record is being patched outside normal workflow;
  - the action should only be used due to a process or workflow bug;
  - the action changes only ticket state;
  - it does not run StateBook, BlueBook, TransitionAction modules, chapter evaluation, orchestration, or governance recalculation.
- `Patch` requires:
  - acknowledgement checkbox;
  - target state selection;
  - remarks/reason;
  - optional evidence attachment.
- `CustomerTicketZTSMAction` handles `RuntimeAction=Patch` by:
  - enforcing IPC permission;
  - validating the target state via `Kernel::System::State`;
  - allowing only `new`, `open`, `pending reminder`, `pending auto`, or `closed` state types;
  - calling `TicketStateSet()` only;
  - writing an audit article with subject `[IPC Patch] Ticket state manually corrected`.
- The audit article records previous state, target state, IPC customer user, and the submitted remarks.
- Synced the focused change across canonical runtime source, GovernanceDB package source, GovernanceDB runtime overlay, `ZTSMOverlay`, and the local `otobo-11.0.16` CustomerTicketZoom copy.

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.272 Follow-up Completion State Handoff Guard

### Completed work

- Fixed the remaining Follow-up completion handoff gap where the child completion article could be posted back to the Diagnosis ticket but the original execution ticket still displayed `follow-up`.
- Root cause: the parent state restore was only performed inside `ZTSMChapterDirector`; if that path did not finish cleanly after customer task completion, the article existed but the parent state could remain stuck.
- `CustomerTicketZTSMAction::CompleteTask` now runs a direct follow-up parent completion guard after ChapterDirector:
  - reloads the closed child task;
  - confirms the parent is still in `follow-up`;
  - verifies the BlueLevel is complete;
  - verifies the PurpleBook has no next BlueLevel;
  - moves the original parent ticket back to `in-progress`;
  - writes a `ZTSM Follow-up Completed` article for the state handoff.
- `ZTSMChapterDirector` now checks the `TicketStateSet()` result when restoring the original ticket to `in-progress` and logs an error if the restore fails.

## 2026-07-13 GovernanceDB 0.0.271 Follow-up Task Owner Weightage Backfill

### Completed work

- Fixed the broader follow-up/task completion weightage issue where a task closed as successful could still contribute `0 / 1`.
- Root cause: follow-up tasks created before the latest fixes could be missing `ZTicket-OwnerWeightage`, so closing them as Successful or No Action still left `CurrentWeightage=0`.
- `ZTSMBlueBookRuntime::LevelComplete()` now treats fulfilled closed states as default/required weightage when `ZTicket-OwnerWeightage` is missing:
  - `closed successful`;
  - `diagnosed`;
  - `closed no action`;
  - `closed duplicate`.
- `ZTSMChapterDirector` uses the same fulfilled-closure fallback before deciding whether to generate an additional ChapterPlay.
- `CustomerTicketZTSMAction::CompleteTask` now writes `ZTicket-OwnerWeightage` from `ZTicket-RequiredWeightage` when the task is missing owner weightage at completion time.
- This preserves the intended rule: if the level is genuinely under-filled, spawn another play; if the completed task should fulfill the level, count it correctly.
- Synced the focused change across canonical runtime source, GovernanceDB package source, GovernanceDB runtime overlay, and `ZTSMOverlay`.

## 2026-07-10 GovernanceDB 0.0.257 Profile-Aware PurpleBook Follow-Up Resolver

### Completed work

- Fixed the remaining owned `Diagnosis` child menu issue where `Amend` appeared but `Follow-up` did not.

## 2026-07-10 GovernanceDB 0.0.253 BlueBook Child Ticket Number Collision Fix

### Completed work

- Fixed the Incident Diagnosis same-level BlueBook spawn failure where Cloud child creation succeeded but Network child creation failed during `TicketCreate`.
- Runtime evidence showed BlueBook parsed and evaluated both records, then the second Diagnosis ticket failed with:
  - duplicate `ticket_number_counter_uid`;
  - null `tn` insert;
  - `ZTSMBlueBookReader: TicketCreate failed ... Chapter=BR-002 Type=Diagnosis`.
- Root cause addressed in `Kernel/System/Ticket/Number/TESSERAIdentity.pm`:
  - scoped child counter UIDs for same parent/type could collide because the scoped prefix left a short deterministic suffix;
  - a counter insert collision caused ticket number generation to return no ticket number, so `TicketCreate` tried to insert a null `tn`.
- `TESSERAIdentity.pm` now:
  - generates a random suffix for scoped child counter UIDs;
  - retries scoped counter insertion up to five times before failing.
- Fixed list-context argument collapse in `ZTSMBlueBookReader.pm` by making `_TicketIteration()` scalar-safe before it is used inside hash argument/hash value construction.

## 2026-07-02 GovernanceDB 0.0.203 Override Outcome Weightage and Delegate Acknowledgement

### Architectural Decisions

- MELT keeps GeneralCatalog truth in `ZTSM::MELT::*` namespaces rather than reusing `ITSM::ConfigItem::*` or `ZTSM::GovernanceObject::*`.

### Completed work

## 2026-06-30 GovernanceDB 0.0.181 TESSERA Ticket Identity Number Generator

### Completed work

- Added a first-class TESSERA ticket number generator module: `Kernel::System::Ticket::Number::TESSERAIdentity`.
- New generated ticket format is `SystemIdentity-TypeCode-YearSequence`, for example `ICAT-SE-20260000001` with the default package settings.
- Added SysConfig setting `Ticket::NumberGenerator::TESSERAIdentity` in `ZTSMGovernanceRuntime.xml` with:
  - `SystemIdentity`
  - `TypeCodeLength`
  - `SequencePadding`
  - `SequenceScope`
  - `ResetPolicy`
  - editable `TypeCodes` for `ServiceRequest`, `Change`, `Incident`, `Problem`, `Assessment`, `Approval`, `Task`, `Verification`, `Endorsement`, `FollowUp`, and `Exception`.
- Ticket type code resolution now uses the configured type-code mapping first.
- If no mapping is found, the generator derives an uppercase fallback from the first configured number of alphanumeric characters in the ticket type name, so `Unknown` becomes `UN` when `TypeCodeLength = 2`.
- Updated `TicketCreate()` to pass resolved `TypeID` and `Type` into ticket number generation.
- Updated `Ticket::NumberBase` so hash-style ticket-number context is supported without breaking the old positional offset recursion used by stock generators.
- Implemented yearly sequence numbering over `ticket_number_counter`, using `SequencePadding = 7` by default.
- Mirrored `Ticket.pm`, `NumberBase.pm`, and `TESSERAIdentity.pm` across source, GovernanceDB package source/runtime overlay, local `otobo-11.0.16`, and `ZTSMOverlay`.

## 2026-06-29 ServiceCatalog 11.0.12 Stale Core Preference Cleanup

### Completed work

- Diagnosed why the Admin Service overview could still show the old `TYPE` even after import updated the service timestamp:
  - `ServiceUpdate()` writes the real service type to `service.type_id`;
  - `Kernel::System::Service::ServiceListGet()` reads `service.type_id`, then merges `service_preferences` into the same service hash;

  - marks those definitions out of sync;
  - runs `DefinitionSync()` to create a refreshed ConfigItem definition version with the corrected date range embedded.

## 2026-06-26 GovernanceDB GenericAgent Bootstrap Defer 0.0.156

### Completed work

- Diagnosed the `0.0.155` install log:
  - The base64 install corruption was fixed; files now install as real source.
  - The remaining install-time errors came from `Kernel::System::GovernanceDB::Bootstrap::_GenericAgentJobsEnsure`.
  - `_GenericAgentJobsEnsure` constructed `Kernel::System::GenericAgent` during package post-code.
  - `GenericAgent->new()` validates all dynamic fields, including existing `GovernanceObject` fields.
  - During package install/upgrade, the package's `DynamicFields::Driver###GovernanceObject` SysConfig can be not active yet, causing repeated `Backend GovernanceObject is invalid!` errors.
- Added a bootstrap preflight guard before constructing `Kernel::System::GenericAgent`:
  - If `DynamicFields::Driver->{GovernanceObject}->{Module}` is not active yet, the GenericAgent seed is deferred with a notice.
  - This avoids aborting/noising package installation while preserving idempotent job seeding for a later run when the runtime config is active.
- Bumped `GovernanceDB.sopm` package version to `0.0.156`.
- Rebuilt `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.156.opm`.
- Supersedes `0.0.155`; install/upgrade testing should use `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.156.opm`.
- `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.0.156.opm` SHA256: `AF63D7DDFF67867952620C41B79F594EFE205F3A073465C019676A6E307D2E1D`.

## 2026-06-24 StateBook GeneralCatalog Class Guard 0.0.132

### Completed work

- Fixed the submit-time StateBook resolver failure after `0.0.131` advanced far enough to parse StateBook rows:
  - Runtime error: `Need Class!`
  - Traceback: `Kernel::System::GeneralCatalog::ItemList` called from `ZTSMStateBookReader::_StateNameResolve`.
- Root cause: `_StateNameResolve()` called `GeneralCatalog->ItemList()` whenever the DynamicField type was `GeneralCatalog`, even when the DynamicField config did not contain `Config->{Class}`. OTOBO requires `Class`, so the submit transaction failed before BlueBook orchestration could continue.

## Architectural Decisions

- Additional stakeholder injection is a runtime execution action, not a StateBook transition.
- Additional stakeholder injection is not BlueBook choreography; BlueBook already defines the planned sequence.
- The action is controlled by Ticket Type, not lifecycle state.
- Allowed hardcoded Ticket Types for now: `Assessment`, `Endorsement`, `Approval`.
- Future control can move to SysConfig or a governance object, but current implementation intentionally keeps the rule local and explicit.
- The action must not modify governance snapshots, lifecycle position, StateBook position, or BlueBook position.
- The additional task duplicates execution evidence only; it does not duplicate governance truth.
- Closed execution child tickets must not allow additional mandatory stakeholders, to avoid hanging a gate after work has already completed.
- Existing BlueBook level completion logic blocks progression while any child in the same parent, BlueBook, and BlueLevel remains open, so the new mandatory child naturally prevents lifecycle advancement until completed.
- External-party request creation is a separate root/governance request clone, not a child execution duplicate.
- External-party request creation goes back through ServiceLibrarian after cloning, because the selected service can represent a different vendor or party.
- If the cloned request already carries `ZTicket-StateBook`, ServiceLibrarian must treat the snapshot as already chosen and must not resolve governance again.
- Parent/request Dynamic Fields are copied through Dynamic Field backend APIs, not string-rendered values, so DynamicField Set data stays structured.
- `closed no action` and `closed duplicate` are not failure states.
- A neutral closure only propagates upward when it represents the whole mandatory BlueLevel; otherwise it behaves as completion evidence for its own child ticket.
- Assessment neutral closure is an assessor task outcome, not a requester action.
- Assessment neutral closure uses the same owner enforcement as normal Assessment submission.
- Task completion is an implementer task outcome, not a requester action.
- `ZTicket-Result` is the Task details field.
- Parent request status evidence is represented by `ZTicket-Outcome`; hard-stop negative outcomes additionally close the parent ticket state.
- Follow-up is a runtime corrective execution action, not a StateBook transition.
- PurpleBook is read from the current BlueBook record using `ZBlue-PurpleBook`; no ticket Dynamic Field was introduced for PurpleBook.
- Template is read from the current BlueBook record using `ZBlue-Template`; no ticket Dynamic Field was introduced for Template.
- PurpleBook child tickets use their PurpleBook as `ZTicket-BlueBook` and the original child ticket as `ZTicket-Parent`.
- Successful PurpleBook completion returns the original child to `in-progress`; it does not resume StateBook directly.
- Failed mandatory PurpleBook completion propagates through the original child so the original parent BlueBook receives failed-first handling.
- Template risk assessment hydration uses existing `ZRM-*` ticket fields because the current risk assessment workspace stores ticket risk rows there.
- Mandatory outcome precedence:
  - Rollback outranks Failed.
  - Failed outranks Partial Success.
  - Partial Success outranks Successful/No Action but does not stop BlueBook flow.
  - Only mandatory child tickets affect parent outcome roll-up.

## Rejected Approaches

- Do not enable by `ZState-CurrentState`; Ticket Type is the cleaner action-control layer.
- Do not make this a StateBook transition.
- Do not make this a BlueBook transition.
- Do not recalculate governance or rebuild snapshots when adding the stakeholder.
- Do not introduce new Dynamic Field names for this behavior.
- Do not allow additions on closed child tickets.
- Do not make external-party request creation a BlueBook or StateBook transition.
- Do not duplicate child execution tickets for the external-party request; create a new root request and let runtime orchestration handle it.
- Do not force ServiceSupportMap re-resolution when `ZTicket-StateBook` is already present.
- Do not treat `closed no action` or `closed duplicate` as mandatory failure.
- Do not close the parent/root ticket when other tasks exist in the same BlueBook level.
- Do not expose `closed duplicate` or `closed no action` as generic outcomes for Endorsement or Approval yet; current requirement is Assessment/Assessor only.
- Do not use Task free-text remarks as the canonical result; store Task details in `ZTicket-Result`.
- Do not let non-mandatory child outcomes drive parent outcome roll-up.
- Do not show Follow-up when the BlueBook record has no `ZBlue-PurpleBook`.
- Do not store PurpleBook or Template on new `ZTicket-*` fields.
- Do not let PurpleBook spawning overwrite the original child ticket BlueLevel.

- Assessment `Duplicate` and `No Action` are assessor-owned outcome submissions for the current assessment child, not separate top-level requester actions.

## 2026-06-17 Customer Request Hydration / Follow-up Ownership Design

### Architectural Decisions

* Customer request defaults are requester convenience values, not governance truth.
* Customer defaults are stored on the CustomerUser object through:

  * `ZUser-Application`
  * `ZUser-Environment`
  * `ZUser-Location`
  * `ZUser-SupportProfile`
* Request defaults should automatically hydrate new root governance requests during customer ticket creation.
* Hydration occurs only when the ticket field is empty; explicitly supplied ticket values always win.
* User defaults are snapshots at request creation time and must not remain linked to the CustomerUser record after ticket creation.
* Follow-up remains a runtime corrective execution action and not a StateBook transition.
* Follow-up child tickets inherit execution ownership context from the initiating child ticket.
* PurpleBook execution must preserve ownership continuity so the initiating owner can continue the corrective workflow without reassignment surprises.
* Successful PurpleBook completion returns the original child ticket to its previous execution owner and execution group.

### Completed Design

#### Customer Request Default Hydration

When a new customer request is created:

* `ZUser-Application` hydrates `ZTicket-Application`.
* `ZUser-Environment` hydrates `ZTicket-Env`.
* `ZUser-Location` hydrates `ZTicket-Location`.
* `ZUser-SupportProfile` remains requester preference context and is not automatically written to execution ownership fields.

#### Multi-Value Handling

Customer preference fields are currently single-select.

Ticket fields may be multi-select.

Hydration rules:

* Single → Single:

  * Copy value directly.
* Single → Multi:

  * Wrap value as a single-item array.
* Empty User Value:

  * Do not write ticket value.
* Existing Ticket Value:

  * Do not overwrite.

Example:

Customer:

* `ZUser-Location = Singapore DC`

Ticket:

* `ZTicket-Location` supports multiple values

Result:

* `["Singapore DC"]`

#### Follow-up Ownership Propagation

When Follow-up is executed:

Source Child Ticket:

* `ZTicket-Owner`
* `ZTicket-OwnerGroup`

must be copied to newly created PurpleBook child tickets.

This preserves:

* Visibility
* Ownership continuity
* Runtime action permissions
* Corrective execution accountability

#### Follow-up Return Ownership

When PurpleBook execution completes successfully:

* Original child ticket returns to `in-progress`.
* Original child ticket retains:

  * `ZTicket-Owner`
  * `ZTicket-OwnerGroup`

PurpleBook completion must not:

* Reassign ownership.
* Clear ownership.
* Replace ownership with PurpleBook executor values.

### Rejected Approaches

* Do not force customers to repeatedly select Application, Environment, and Location for every request when defaults already exist.
* Do not overwrite explicitly supplied ticket values using CustomerUser defaults.
* Do not link tickets dynamically back to CustomerUser defaults after ticket creation.
* Do not create new ownership fields for PurpleBook execution.
* Do not recalculate ownership during PurpleBook return.
* Do not transfer ownership to the last PurpleBook executor when returning to the original child ticket.

### Next Priorities

* Implement CustomerTicketMessage hydration from CustomerUser defaults.
* Verify single-value to multi-value field conversion behavior.
* Verify new customer requests receive default Application, Environment, and Location values.
* Verify Follow-up child tickets inherit Owner and OwnerGroup.
* Verify PurpleBook successful completion returns original child tickets to the same Owner and OwnerGroup.
* Verify all runtime action visibility rules continue to function after ownership propagation.

  - Runtime warning: `Odd number of elements in hash assignment ... ZTSMStateBookReader.pm line 114`

- Once the offending GenericAgent job is identified and corrected at source, consider removing the runtime guard or reducing its log level.

## 2026-08-04 MELT ConfigItem Definition Isolation 0.0.7

- Forensic review of MELT `0.0.2` through `0.0.6` found no deletion of `configitem`, `configitem_version`, or `configitem_definition` records. Preview builds copied ConfigItems into MELT tables; `0.0.6` cleanup deletes only MELT-owned runtime tables.
- Found an invalid cross-package mutation in every MELT bootstrap through `0.0.6`: `_ITSMConfigItemLifecycleDateDynamicFieldsEnsure()` updated five ITSM ConfigItem Date DynamicFields and forced `DefinitionSetOutOfSync()` plus `DefinitionSync()` for affected classes.
- OTOBO `DefinitionSync()` preserves the prior class definition and inserts a new version through `DefinitionAdd()`; it does not delete the earlier JSON/YAML definition. The missing Overview content is therefore tracked as a rendering/runtime failure, not proven data destruction.
- Removed the lifecycle-date ConfigItem mutation and its helper from MELT. MELT install and upgrade no longer call ITSM ConfigItem definition synchronization or clean the ConfigItem definition cache.
- Built `Kernel/Package/MELT-0.0.7.opm`; SHA256 `EE5485057C07729E234274BE3F3CF6589CED11FD0BC8F97A656CF3A19D7C356C`.
- Validation passed: Bootstrap Perl syntax, 96 byte-matching OPM payloads, and the packaged Bootstrap contains no lifecycle ConfigItem sync/cache mutation.

## 2026-08-11 GovernanceObject/MELT Class-and-Name Duplicate Choice 0.1.108 / 0.0.14

- GovernanceObject and MELT workbook imports use only case-insensitive `Class + Name` duplicate detection when Number is empty; they do not use ConfigItem Application, Environment, or Location fields.
- A duplicate is presented for explicit confirmation: Update merges into the selected numbered object, Skip leaves it unchanged, and Create makes a separate object.
- When Create is selected for an occupied class/name, the importer assigns the next available name using `Name - 2`, `Name - 3`, and so on.

- Perl and JavaScript syntax validation passed, and `git diff --check` reported no errors.
## 2026-08-11 CMDB Best-Effort Duplicate Identity 0.1.109

- CMDB workbook duplicate matching always uses case-insensitive ConfigItem `Class + Name`.
- It additionally compares only identity fields actually present in the selected class's effective definition: `ZTAM-Application`, `ZTAM-Environment`, and `ZTAM-Location`.
- Classes defining none of those fields fall back to `Class + Name`; classes defining a subset use only that subset.
- Empty incoming identity values are treated as unavailable matching evidence rather than as proof of difference. A possible match is therefore still shown, and clearing existing populated data requires the existing `UPDATE_CLEAR` confirmation.
- Built `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.109.opm`; SHA256 `12005538E81F49644F60E84F2BF1ED4199757923E6F0F4AD43481090C59E5EF8`.
## 2026-08-11 CMDB Asset-Tag Differentiation 0.1.110

- Added `ZTAM-AssetTag` as a strong negative duplicate signal for workbook import.
- When both the existing ConfigItem and incoming row have non-empty asset tags and the values differ case-insensitively, they are treated as different assets and no merge candidate is offered.
- When either asset tag is empty, matching continues using the class-defined best-effort identity criteria.
- An explicit CMDB Number remains authoritative for intentional updates.
- Built `Kernel/Package/GovernanceDB-0.1.110.opm`; SHA256 `56C5226F82B086BDF35DB10DC3DF1193AE389B91C6A1C7D3AB573F9D557CCD40`.
